title: NDA review checklist

source.work: NDA Review 1.0.0 (assistant-workflows/nda-review/SKILL.md), author Open Legal Products

changes: The sixteen checklist rows are ported word for word. The workflow's instruction to flag drafting errors is added as a seventeenth item, Drafting consistency. Its risk ratings and its single result table are left out: here each item gets one verdict, and findings are split into legal issues and commercial preferences, as in the same repository's dpa-review workflow.

items.title: Parties
items.general: Identify each party and their role. Confirm whether the NDA is mutual or one-way and that obligations are correctly allocated. Flag missing affiliates, mismatched roles, or obligations inconsistent with the agreed structure.

items.title: Purpose
items.general: Summarize the permitted purpose for which confidential information may be used.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag overly broad purpose language that permits use beyond the intended transaction.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag unclear or narrow purpose that prevents legitimate use of information in connection with the transaction.

items.title: Definition of Confidential Information
items.general: Explain what information is protected, including oral, visual, derived, or pre-existing information.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag definitions too narrow to protect all disclosed information, or no protection for oral or unmarked information.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag definitions overbroad, capturing publicly available information or information not actually sensitive.

items.title: Exclusions
items.general: Identify standard exclusions such as public domain, independently developed, already known, or third-party received information.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag missing standard exclusions that would allow the receiving party to escape obligations too easily.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag missing standard exclusions (public domain, independently developed, already known) or exclusions that are too difficult to prove.

items.title: Disclosure Obligations
items.general: Summarize confidentiality obligations, standard of care, and use or disclosure restrictions.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag standards of care too weak to adequately protect the information.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag strict liability, vague standards, or obligations higher than own-information standards that expose the receiving party disproportionately.

items.title: Permitted Recipients
items.general: Identify who may receive confidential information, including affiliates, representatives, advisers, financing sources, or investors.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag recipient categories too broad, or no requirement for recipients to be bound by equivalent obligations.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag missing adviser, affiliate, or financing source access rights needed to evaluate the transaction.

items.title: Recipient Liability
items.general: State whether the receiving party is responsible for breaches by permitted recipients.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag absence of receiving party responsibility for breaches by permitted recipients.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag uncapped liability for actions of recipients outside the party's direct control.

items.title: Compelled Disclosure
items.general: Summarize disclosure required by law, regulation, court order, stock exchange, or governmental authority.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag no notice right, no cooperation obligation, or overly broad compelled disclosure permissions.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag overly burdensome notice requirements or obligations to resist disclosure beyond what is practicable.

items.title: Term
items.general: State the agreement term and the duration of confidentiality obligations.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag obligations that expire too soon or unclear continuation of obligations after agreement end.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag indefinite obligations or unusually long terms for non-trade-secret information.

items.title: Return or Destruction
items.general: Summarize return, destruction, retention, and archival copy obligations.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag no return obligation or inadequate destruction mechanics.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag no carve-out for archival, compliance, backup, or legal retention copies.

items.title: Residual Knowledge
items.general: Identify whether unaided memory or residual knowledge may be used.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag broad residual knowledge rights that could undermine confidentiality protections.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag absence of a residual knowledge carve-out that prevents legitimate use of unaided memory.

items.title: Non-Solicit / Standstill
items.general: Identify non-solicitation, non-circumvention, standstill, exclusivity, or similar restrictions.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag absence of non-solicitation or standstill protections where commercially expected.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag hidden restrictive covenants, long durations, broad covered persons, or restrictions unrelated to confidentiality.

items.title: No Warranty / No Obligation
items.general: Summarize disclaimers about accuracy, completeness, warranties, or obligation to proceed.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag missing disclaimers that could create liability for the accuracy or completeness of disclosed information.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag disclaimers that conflict with fraud or intentional misrepresentation, or that expressly exclude reliance.

items.title: Remedies
items.general: Identify injunctive relief, equitable remedies, indemnities, liquidated damages, or enforcement provisions.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag absence of injunctive relief or inadequate remedies for breach.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag automatic injunction language, broad indemnities, or liquidated damages without adequate safeguards.

items.title: Assignment
items.general: Summarize restrictions on assignment or transfer.

sides.Disclosing Party: Flag free assignment rights that could transfer obligations to unknown parties.
sides.Receiving Party: Flag restrictions that block legitimate affiliate transfers needed for the deal process.

items.title: Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
items.general: State governing law, forum, arbitration provisions, and submission to jurisdiction. Flag unfamiliar law, asymmetric process, inconvenient forum, or missing service provisions.

items.title: Drafting Consistency
items.general: Flag general drafting errors that may affect the represented party, including inconsistent defined terms, inconsistent entity names, cross-reference errors, numbering issues, duplicated provisions, missing schedules, and internal inconsistencies.
